exitProficiencyTarget: Novice High by grade 8 (banks the full 2-credit WA graduation requirement), stretch Intermediate Low
standardsBasis: Program-design target per expansion-plan-2026-09 §3 B1: WA competency-based credit crosswalk (RCW 28A.230.090 — Novice High = 2 credits); OSPI recommends proficiency testing at end of grade 8. Standard tags use WA's 2015 World Languages standard numbers (5 Cs). Sub-standard numbering verified 2026-09-05 against the primary source (OSPI v1.3 PDF, p.6, "II. World Languages Learning Standards"): 1.1 Interpersonal/1.2 Interpretive/1.3 Presentational Communication; 2.1 Relating Cultural Practices/2.2 Relating Cultural Products to Perspectives; 3.1 Making Connections/3.2 Acquiring Information and Diverse Perspectives; 4.1 Language/4.2 Cultural Comparisons; 5.1 School and Global Communities/5.2 Lifelong Learning.
bandNotes: First systematically grammar-supported band: full present tense (regular, stem-changing, reflexive), tener idioms, ser/estar, gustar-type verbs, and a preterite introduction in the final third (the Intermediate Low stretch — creating with language about past events). Weekly output moves from memorized frames to original strung-together sentences and short paragraphs. Review weeks are framed as integrated performance assessments (interpretive + interpersonal + presentational). Assumes no prior Spanish; earlier-band vocabulary reappears inside new structures.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — greeting peers and adults with the right register
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Greeting exchange rounds; when do Spanish speakers use tú vs. usted?
Day 2: Register sort — which greeting for your friend, your teacher, a store clerk?
Day 3: Role-play stations: greet a principal (usted) vs. a teammate (tú).
Day 4: Listening — identify formal vs. informal conversations from audio clips.
Day 5: Skit performance: one formal and one informal greeting-and-goodbye exchange.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — exchanging origin and nationality
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Nationality adjectives — pattern-spot the -o/-a and -ense endings.
Day 2: Famous Spanish speakers guess-who with nationality clues.
Day 3: Interview circuit: '¿De dónde eres?' '¿Dónde naciste?' with world map pins.
Day 4: Read short identity bios of four teens from different countries.
Day 5: Write and share your own 4-line identity bio.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — geography and demographics of the Spanish-speaking world
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Map the 21 countries where Spanish is official; label continents and regions.
Day 2: Population data dive — rank the five biggest Spanish-speaking countries (math link).
Day 3: Spanish in the US — where and how many? Washington state data spotlight.
Day 4: Country trading-cards — each student builds a card (capital, region, población).
Day 5: Card-swap quiz game using the class deck.

weeks.topic: Subject pronouns & ser; ustedes vs. vosotros
weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — pronoun systems across Spanish varieties and English
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Pronoun chart build; ser conjugation song (soy, eres, es, somos, son).
Day 2: Pronoun swap drills — replace names with él/ella/ellos.
Day 3: Dialect discovery: Latin America uses ustedes (our course standard); Spain uses vosotros; Argentina says vos — hear all three.
Day 4: Sentence building with ser — identity, origin, profession, description.
Day 5: Mini-quiz + reflection: which pronoun would you use with whom, where?

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing personality with agreement
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Personality vocabulary with celebrity/character examples; agreement rules (o/a, singular/plural).
Day 2: 'Yo soy... pero mi amigo es...' contrast sentences.
Day 3: Personality quiz in Spanish; tally class results.
Day 4: Write a description of a friend or family member (4-5 sentences).
Day 5: Read descriptions aloud; class matches to photos/drawings.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — reading class schedules and school documents
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Ordinal numbers + class periods; describe your real schedule.
Day 2: Read two authentic-style school schedules from Latin America; answer comprehension questions.
Day 3: Opinion exchange — '¿Qué materia es interesante? ¿Aburrida?' with reasons.
Day 4: Time + subject integration: 'Tengo ciencias a las diez.'
Day 5: Design your dream schedule and defend one choice to the class.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — discussing daily activities with -ar verbs
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: The -ar conjugation pattern — one pattern unlocks hundreds of verbs.
Day 2: Conjugation relay races; accuracy over speed round two.
Day 3: 'Find someone who...' survey — estudia mucho, trabaja en casa, mira deportes.
Day 4: Write 6 sentences about what your family members do daily.
Day 5: Partner interviews and third-person report-outs.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — understanding short texts about student life
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: -er/-ir patterns beside -ar; spot what changes and what doesn't.
Day 2: Verb-ending sort race with mixed infinitives.
Day 3: Read a pen-pal letter about a student's life; annotate every verb.
Day 4: Comprehension + response — answer the pen pal in 5 sentences.
Day 5: Class verb bee — conjugate on the spot, spelling counts.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — negotiating plans around likes and dislikes
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Gustar mechanics — me gusta/me gustan; why 'it pleases me' explains everything.
Day 2: Free-time preference survey with singular/plural gustar accuracy.
Day 3: 'A mí también / a mí no' agreement-disagreement exchanges.
Day 4: Plan a weekend with a partner both of you would actually enjoy.
Day 5: Present your plan; class votes for best weekend.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — keeping a conversation going with questions
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Question-word wall + accent marks matter (que vs. qué).
Day 2: Question-formation drills from statements.
Day 3: 20-preguntas guessing game.
Day 4: Interview a classmate with 6 original questions; take notes.
Day 5: Report the interview in third person; audience asks one follow-up.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — extended family bonds and multigenerational homes
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Extended-family tree vocabulary + possessives (mi/tu/su).
Day 2: Family riddles — 'el hijo de mi tía es mi...'.
Day 3: Multigenerational households and compadrazgo (godparent bonds) in Latin America; compare family gatherings.
Day 4: Describe two relatives: appearance, personality, mayor/menor.
Day 5: Family presentation with a drawn or digital tree.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Language Comparisons — idioms that don't translate word-for-word
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Why Spanish 'has' hunger while English 'is' hungry — idiom mindset.
Day 2: Situation cards — respond with the right tener expression.
Day 3: Tener que + infinitive — obligations list for a school week.
Day 4: Comic strip: a character's day told through tener expressions.
Day 5: Idiom charades tournament.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Listening — locating people and things from spoken descriptions
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Ser (what it IS) vs. estar (how/where it is) — sort sentence cards.
Day 2: Preposition TPR — place objects encima de/debajo de on command.
Day 3: Listen-and-draw — position items in a room from audio only.
Day 4: Describe-the-room writing: 5 sentences with está + preposition.
Day 5: Barrier game — partners recreate each other's object layouts by speaking only.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — tracking your own proficiency with can-do statements
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Stations review — verbs, family, questions, ser/estar games.
Day 2: Interpretive check — reading and listening tasks across weeks 1-13.
Day 3: Interpersonal check — recorded partner conversation on familiar topics.
Day 4: Presentational check — short spoken self-introduction, polished.
Day 5: Can-do reflection ('puedo presentarme', 'todavía no...') + one metas-setting conference.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Practices to Perspectives — dining out, ordering, and tipping customs
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Restaurant vocabulary + el mesero (Latin American usage) vs. el camarero (Spain).
Day 2: Read an authentic-style menu; plan a full order within a budget.
Day 3: Ordering scripts — polite requests, questions about dishes.
Day 4: Tipping and dining customs across Latin America; la sobremesa (lingering after the meal).
Day 5: Full restaurant simulation — rotate roles: mesero, clientes, cajero.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — presenting weekend and vacation plans
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Ir conjugation + a/al/a la contractions; destination flashcards.
Day 2: '¿Adónde vas?' chain interviews around the room.
Day 3: Ir a + infinitive = near future — 'Voy a nadar el sábado.'
Day 4: Draft a weekend-plans monologue (destinations + future activities).
Day 5: Deliver plans to the class; audience notes one detail per speaker.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — understanding texts with high-frequency irregular verbs
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: The e→ie shoe-verb pattern (querer, pensar, empezar, entender, preferir).
Day 2: The o→ue pattern (poder, dormir, almorzar); mixed drills.
Day 3: Preference interviews — '¿Qué prefieres...?' with report-backs.
Day 4: Read a day-in-the-life text dense with stem-changers; annotate the changes.
Day 5: Stem-change board-game review in teams.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — demonstrating all three modes at midyear
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: IPA overview + rubric walkthrough; warm-up tasks in all three modes.
Day 2: Interpretive task — authentic-style reading and listening set.
Day 3: Interpersonal task — unrehearsed partner conversation from a familiar-topic prompt.
Day 4: Presentational task — prepared 60-second talk with visuals.
Day 5: Results conferences + goal adjustments for the spring semester.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — fashion, markets, and smart shopping
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Clothing review + shopping vocabulary; describe today's outfits.
Day 2: Store dialogues — sizes, colors, trying things on.
Day 3: Mercado vs. mall — where teens shop across Latin America.
Day 4: Catalog challenge — 'buy' an outfit within a peso budget (recycles numbers).
Day 5: Shopping role-play marathon with rotating clerk/customer pairs.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — currencies and exchange rates (math/economics link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Hundreds and thousands — say and write big numbers accurately.
Day 2: Currency tour — whose money features a bird? A volcano? Currency-country match.
Day 3: Exchange-rate math — convert a $20 allowance into pesos, soles, quetzales.
Day 4: Price-is-right game with real-world LatAm prices.
Day 5: Budget project — plan a day in Mexico City on 500 pesos.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — describing your home and responsibilities
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Home vocabulary expansion; el patio in Latin American home design.
Day 2: Chore negotiations — 'Debo... pero puedo...' obligation vs. ability.
Day 3: Room description writing with location prepositions (recycles week 13).
Day 4: Design a fair family chore schedule; justify it.
Day 5: Home-and-chores presentation with a floor plan visual.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — climate zones and hemispheres (earth science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Weather review + forecast vocabulary; Celsius vs. Fahrenheit conversions.
Day 2: December in Buenos Aires is summer — hemisphere flip investigation.
Day 3: Tropical climates — dry/rainy seasons replace four seasons near the equator.
Day 4: Read real forecasts from three cities; chart and compare.
Day 5: Deliver a two-city comparative weather report.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — fútbol as a cultural force
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Sports vocabulary + la cancha (Latin American usage); favorite-team talk.
Day 2: Why the Copa Mundial stops traffic from Mexico to Argentina.
Day 3: Listen to match-commentary clips; track the score and key words.
Day 4: Player profile — write a mini-bio of an athlete from a Spanish-speaking country.
Day 5: Present player profiles; class builds a dream team.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — narrating a full day with reflexive verbs
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Reflexive pronoun mechanics — me ducho, te duchas; act the routine.
Day 2: Sequence your real day with antes de/después de connectors.
Day 3: Compare routines with a partner; find three differences.
Day 4: Write a full-day narration (morning to acostarse), 8+ sentences.
Day 5: Routine narrations performed with mime accompaniment.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpersonal Communication — describing symptoms and giving simple advice
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Body review + illness vocabulary; me duele mechanics (like gustar).
Day 2: Symptom charades — '¿Qué te duele?' diagnosis game.
Day 3: Doctor-visit dialogues — describe symptoms, receive advice (debes descansar).
Day 4: Health-advice poster — remedies for a cold in Spanish.
Day 5: Clinic role-play day with rotating doctor/patient pairs.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — using Spanish safely in online spaces
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Tech vocabulary — el celular and la computadora (Latin American usage).
Day 2: Spanish-language media in your pocket: music, shows, and apps you can switch to Spanish.
Day 3: Digital safety in Spanish — strong contraseñas, what not to share (digital-literacy link).
Day 4: Write text-message dialogues in Spanish with common abbreviations.
Day 5: Pitch: one Spanish-language song/show/app the class should try, and why.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — entertainment that travels the Spanish-speaking world
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Genre vocabulary; poll the class's favorite géneros.
Day 2: The telenovela phenomenon — why the whole family watches.
Day 3: Music map — reguetón, cumbia, mariachi, bachata origins by region.
Day 4: Review writing — rate a song or show in Spanish (me encanta porque...).
Day 5: Class awards show — present 'best of' picks with short justifications.

weeks.actflFocus: Presentational Speaking — narrating past events in sequence (Intermediate Low stretch)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: -ar preterite endings — hablé, hablaste, habló; timeline anchors (ayer, anoche).
Day 2: 'What did you do yesterday?' interviews with -ar verbs.
Day 3: Sequenced narration — primero... luego... finalmente... about last weekend.
Day 4: Write an 8-sentence past-tense diary entry.
Day 5: Story-chain game — each student adds one past-tense sentence.

weeks.actflFocus: Interpretive Reading — following a travel narrative in the past tense
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: -er/-ir preterite endings (comí, viví); travel vocabulary.
Day 2: Read a teen's travel-blog entry about a trip to Costa Rica; sequence the events.
Day 3: Airport process role-play — check-in, la aduana, boarding, in order.
Day 4: Comprehension deep-dive — answer and write questions about the blog text.
Day 5: Write your own 6-8 sentence imagined trip narrative in the preterite.

weeks.actflFocus: Cultures: Products to Perspectives — coffee, cumbia, and Colombian pride
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Colombia geography — two oceans, three cordilleras, one megadiverse country.
Day 2: Coffee country — how el café travels from Colombian farms to Seattle cups.
Day 3: Cumbia listening + Carnaval de Barranquilla highlights.
Day 4: Read a short interview with a Colombian teen; note daily-life details.
Day 5: Colombia showcase — teams present a region, food, or tradition.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Acquiring Information & Diverse Perspectives — Maya civilization through Guatemalan voices
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Maya civilization overview — Tikal, mathematics (they used zero!), the calendar.
Day 2: Living heritage — over 20 Mayan languages spoken in Guatemala today alongside Spanish.
Day 3: Textile study — reading the patterns and towns woven into huipiles.
Day 4: Perspective reading — a Guatemalan student describes market day in her town.
Day 5: Reflect and present: one thing the Maya world teaches us, in Spanish sentences.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Making Connections — ecosystems and conservation (science link)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Environment vocabulary; map megadiverse Spanish-speaking countries.
Day 2: Endangered species profiles — el jaguar, la vaquita, el cóndor.
Day 3: Costa Rica case study — a country running on renewable energy.
Day 4: Write an eco-pledge list — 'Debo reciclar...' (recycles deber).
Day 5: Mini eco-campaign posters in Spanish; gallery walk.

weeks.actflFocus: Connections: Acquiring Information & Diverse Perspectives — biographies from Spanish-language sources
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Read a short Spanish biography of César Chávez; timeline his life (preterite in action).
Day 2: Meet more history-makers — Frida Kahlo, Roberto Clemente, Rigoberta Menchú.
Day 3: Biography jigsaw — teams read different figures, share key events.
Day 4: Write a 6-sentence past-tense biography of a hero you choose.
Day 5: Hero hall — present biographies; class asks when/where questions.

weeks.actflFocus: Comparisons: Cultural Comparisons — adolescence across cultures (and the colegio false friend)
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: False friends alert — el colegio, asistir, la carpeta; build a false-friends wall.
Day 2: Read/watch teen daily-life accounts from two countries; note routines.
Day 3: La quinceañera — the celebration of turning fifteen; compare coming-of-age traditions.
Day 4: Venn-diagram essay draft — teen life: igual y diferente.
Day 5: Structured class discussion — which differences surprised you and why?

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: School & Global Communities — organizing a service project in Spanish
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Brainstorm service ideas that could use Spanish (bilingual signage, welcome guides, food-drive outreach).
Day 2: Plan the campaign — roles, materials, timeline, all discussed in Spanish.
Day 3: Produce bilingual materials — posters, anuncios, social-style posts.
Day 4: Execute or simulate the event; document with Spanish captions.
Day 5: Debrief in Spanish — what worked, what to improve, thank-you notes.

weeks.actflFocus: Communities: Lifelong Learning — proving Novice High and planning the path to the Seal of Biliteracy
lessonBreakdown: Day 1: Assemble the year portfolio — best work from each mode, labeled in Spanish.
Day 2: Final IPA — interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational tasks at Novice High targets.
Day 3: Write the year reflection — logros, challenges, favorite unit.
Day 4: Portfolio conferences — present your portfolio one-on-one or in small groups.
Day 5: Celebration + path forward — how 9-12 Spanish leads to the Seal of Biliteracy; set summer Spanish objetivos.
